how: Participants propose a timed build and later explicitly recruit defenders.
Visible contributors rather than nominal subscribers constitute the working group, since even half a percent running the script is presented as sufficient.
Proposed sprite size is limited by the space contributors believe they can find and maintain.
An active contributor temporarily steps away because the work is mentally exhausting, without announcing collective abandonment.
A participant asks whether the shark exists and receives a picture link, while a later participant asks for its coordinates.
Asking for a sprite and proposing a concrete shark instantiate the revised starter role independently of later uptake.

A template supplies a shared target that can be trimmed to avoid conflict with neighbouring art.
Contributors share and run a defence script and suggest throwaway accounts to bypass the ordinary placement wait.
A common target updates every script runner automatically, providing a technical means of coordinating placement changes.
An explicit leader disclaimer coexists with automatically distributed target changes, so absence of appointed command does not imply wholly dispersed practical control.
Contributors fit placing around sleep and work rather than maintaining uninterrupted personal attention.
An invitation moves negotiation toward another chat, while a separate attempt to enter a neighbour's Discord fails.
